requirements.text: Where the rear lamp does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, the rear lamp shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
requirements.quote: Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.

requirements.text: Where the rear lamp is not switched, contains no switches or does not include inductive load, the rear lamp shall not need to be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.quote: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.

requirements.text: If peak detectors are used for measuring radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
requirements.quote: If peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.

requirements.text: The measurements of radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.
requirements.quote: The measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.

requirements.text: Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments that meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1 may be used for conformity measurements of radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp.
requirements.quote: Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments, that meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1, may be used for conformity measurements.

requirements.text: The FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
requirements.quote: FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.

requirements.text: If FFT-based instruments are used, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
requirements.quote: If using FFT-based instruments, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.

requirements.text: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).
requirements.quote: If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).

requirements.text: For emissions generated by brush commutator motors without an electronic control unit, the maximum step size may be increased up to five times the bandwidth.
requirements.quote: For emissions generated by brush commutator motors without an electronic control unit, the maximum step size may be increased up to five times the bandwidth.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the configuration of the rear lamp with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.
requirements.quote: Measurements Unless otherwise specified the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.

requirements.text: The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses of the rear lamp for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.quote: The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.quote: The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: Where the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may divide the frequency range in 14 frequency bands 30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz and perform tests at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band to confirm that the rear lamp meets the requirements of this Annex.
requirements.quote: Alternatively, if the manufacturer provides measurement to data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, the Technical Service may divide the frequency range in 14 frequency bands 30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850- 1,000 MHz and perform tests at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each band to confirm that the ESA meets the requirements of this Annex.

requirements.text: If the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the rear lamp and not to background radiation.
requirements.quote: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.quote: Readings The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.

requirements.text: The test method described in this Annex may be applied to the rear lamp, which may be subsequently fitted to vehicles which comply with Annex 5.
requirements.quote: The test method described in this Annex may be applied to ESAs, which may be subsequently fitted to vehicles, which comply, with Annex 5.

requirements.text: If not otherwise stated in this Annex, the test of the rear lamp shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
requirements.quote: If not otherwise stated in this Annex the test shall be performed according to CISPR 25.

requirements.text: The rear lamp under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
requirements.quote: ESA state during tests The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

requirements.text: The test of the rear lamp shall be performed according to ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
requirements.quote: The test shall be performed according to ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.

requirements.text: Measurements of radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp shall be performed with an average detector.
requirements.quote: Measurements shall be performed with an average detector.

requirements.text: The measurements of radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.
requirements.quote: The measurements shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver.

requirements.text: Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments that meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1 may be used for conformity measurements of radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp.
requirements.quote: Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments, that meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1, may be used for conformity measurements.

requirements.text: When the rear lamp is tested for radiated narrowband electromagnetic emissions, the Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.
requirements.quote: Measurements The Technical Service shall perform the test at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: If the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the rear lamp and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the rear lamp.
requirements.quote: In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.

requirements.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
requirements.quote: Readings The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.

requirements.text: The rear lamp shall comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered: (a) Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) Stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) Reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
requirements.quote: ESAs may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered:

requirements.text: Where the rear lamp is in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the rear lamp shall comply with the requirements of the combination of the Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2 and Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4 at the manufacturer's discretion provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered.
requirements.quote: ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall comply with the requirements of the combination of the Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2 and Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4 at the manufacturer's discretion provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered.

requirements.text: The frequency range and general test conditions for the immunity test of the rear lamp shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
requirements.quote: (Frequency range and general test conditions shall be based on ISO 11452-1).

requirements.text: The test conditions for the rear lamp shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.quote: The test conditions shall be according to ISO 11452-1.

requirements.text: While the rear lamp is under test, the rear lamp shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
requirements.quote: The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.

requirements.text: While the rear lamp is under test, the rear lamp shall be arranged as defined in this Annex unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
requirements.quote: It shall be arranged as defined in this Annex unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.

requirements.text: The test method shall ensure the immunity of the rear lamp to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply and limit conducted transients from the rear lamp to the vehicle power supply.
requirements.quote: General This test method shall ensure the immunity of ESAs to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply and limit conducted transients from ESAs to the vehicle power supply.

requirements.text: The LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be so designed as to be and to remain in good working order when in normal use.
requirements.quote: LED light sources shall be so designed as to be and to remain in good working order when in normal use.

requirements.text: The LED light sources of the rear lamp shall exhibit no fault in design or manufacture.
requirements.quote: They shall moreover exhibit no fault in design or manufacture.

requirements.text: The LED light sources of the rear lamp shall exhibit no scores or spots on their optical surfaces which might impair their efficiency and their optical performance.
requirements.quote: LED light sources shall exhibit no scores or spots on their optical surfaces which might impair their efficiency and their optical performance.

requirements.text: The absence of scores or spots on the optical surfaces of the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be verified when commencing approval testing and when required in the respective paragraphs in this Regulation.
requirements.quote: This shall be verified when commencing approval testing and when required in the respective paragraphs in this Regulation.

requirements.text: When the LED light sources of the rear lamp are tested, the LED light sources shall first be aged at their test voltage for at least forty-eight hours.
requirements.quote: LED light sources shall first be aged at their test voltage for at least forty-eight hours.

requirements.text: Where the LED light sources of the rear lamp are multi-function LED light sources, each function shall be aged separately.
requirements.quote: For multi-function LED light sources, each function shall be aged separately.

requirements.text: The position and dimensions of the light emitting area of the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall conform to the requirements as given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
requirements.quote: The position and dimensions of the light emitting area shall conform to the requirements as given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.

requirements.text: When measured according to the conditions specified in Annex 4, the luminous flux of the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.
requirements.quote: When measured according to the conditions specified in Annex 4, the luminous flux shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of Annex 1.

requirements.text: When measured according to the test conditions specified in Annex 4, the normalized luminous intensity distribution and/or cumulative luminous flux distribution of the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of annex 1.
requirements.quote: When measured according to the test conditions specified in Annex 4, the normalized luminous intensity distribution and/or cumulative luminous flux distribution shall be within the limits given on the relevant data sheet of annex 1.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be specified on the relevant data sheet.
requirements.quote: The colour of the light emitted by the LED light sources shall be specified on the relevant data sheet.

requirements.text: The definitions of the colour of the light emitted given in Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for type approval shall apply to the LED light sources of the rear lamp.
requirements.quote: The definitions of the colour of the light emitted given in Regulation No. 48 and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for type approval shall apply to this regulation.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be measured by the method specified in Annex 4.
requirements.quote: The colour of the light emitted shall be measured by the method specified in Annex 4.

requirements.text: The measured integral value of the chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall lie within the required chromaticity area.
requirements.quote: The measured integral value of the chromaticity coordinates shall lie within the required chromaticity area.

requirements.text: The minimum red content value of the light emitted by the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be calculated using intervals of one nanometer.
requirements.quote: This value shall be calculated using intervals of one nanometer.

requirements.text: The UV-radiation value of the LED light sources of the rear lamp shall be calculated using intervals of one nanometer.
requirements.quote: This value shall be calculated using intervals of one nanometer.

regulations.rationale: R148 approves the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp. It is the consolidated regulation that replaces R7 and R23. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to the following light-signalling devices (lamps): • Rear-registration plate illuminating lamps • Direction indicator lamps • Position lamps • Stop lamps • End-outline marker lamps • Reversing lamps • Manoeuvring... Spec terms 12.1, obligation base 12.9.)

The lamp is installed on an M1 vehicle, so R48 is the installation regulation for lighting and light-signalling devices. (Installation regulation. Scope: This Regulation applies to vehicles of categories M, N, and to their trailers (category O) with regard to the installation of lighting and light-signalling devices. Spec terms 30.1, obligation base 36.2.)

The integrated retro-reflector is approved under R150, which consolidates R3. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to retro-reflective devices as: • Retro-reflectors of the Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA • Retro-reflective Marking Materials of the Classes C, D, E and F, D/E • Retro-reflective Marking Plates for Heavy and L... Spec terms 3.9, obligation base 3.1.)

The LED modules on a PCB make the lamp an electrical/electronic sub-assembly, so R10 (electromagnetic compatibility) applies. (Electromagnetic compatibility. Scope: This Regulation applies to: Vehicles of categories L, M, N O, T, R and S1 with regard to electromagnetic compatibility; Components and separate technical units intended to be fitted in these vehicles with the limitation given in paragrap... Spec terms 9.3, obligation base 8.0.)

The light sources are LEDs. R128 covers replaceable LED light sources, but LED modules on a PCB are often non-replaceable and approved together with the lamp. I include it because recall matters more than precision. (Light sources. Scope: This Regulation applies to LED light sources shown in Annex 1 and intended for use in approved lamps of power-driven vehicles and of their trailers. Spec terms 8.5, obligation base 9.4.)

R7 has been consolidated into R148, so cite R148 instead. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to: Front and rear position lamps and stop lamps for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O and T; and, End-outline marker lamps for vehicles of categories M, N, O and T. Consolidated into UN R148. Spec terms 1.5, obligation base 2.1.)

R23 has been consolidated into R148. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to: (a) Reversing lamps for vehicles of categories M, N, O, and T; (b) Manoeuvring lamps for vehicles of categories M and N. Consolidated into UN R148. Spec terms 1.5, obligation base 1.2.)

R3 has been consolidated into R150. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to retro-reflecting devices for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O, and T. Consolidated into UN R150. Spec terms 0.4, obligation base 0.0.)

R26 is a vehicle-level regulation on external projections and does not approve the lamp itself. (Vehicle approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to external projections of category M1 vehicles. It does not apply to exterior devices for indirect vision or to the ball of towing devices. The purpose of this Regulation is to reduce the risk or seriousness of b... Spec terms 0.4, obligation base 0.0.)

R37 covers filament light sources, and this lamp uses LEDs. (Light sources. Scope: This Regulation applies to filament light sources and their LED replacement light sources shown in Annex 1 and intended for use in approved lamps of power-driven vehicles and of their trailers. Spec terms 0.4, obligation base 9.4.)

R13H is a braking system regulation. Stop lamp activation is a vehicle braking topic, not a requirement on the lamp. (Vehicle approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to the braking of vehicles of categories M1 and N1. This Regulation does not cover: Spec terms 0.4, obligation base 0.0.)

R149 covers road illumination devices such as headlamps and fog lamps, which this lamp does not include. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to the following road illumination devices (lamps): • Headlamps emitting a driving-beam and/or an asymmetrical passing-beam for vehicles of categories L, M, N and T • Adaptive front-lighting systems (AFS) for vehi... Spec terms 4.2, obligation base 1.6.)

R43 explicitly excludes glazing for lighting devices. (Installation regulation. Scope: This Regulation applies to: (a) Safety glazing materials intended for installation as windscreens or other panes, or as partitioning, on vehicles of category L with bodywork, M, N, O, and T1; (b) Vehicles of category M, N and O with rega... Spec terms 2.8, obligation base 2.0.)

The lamp has no rear fog lamp, and R38 is superseded. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to rear fog lamps for vehicles of categories L3, L4, L5, L7, M, N, O, and T1. Consolidated into UN R148. Spec terms 0.7, obligation base 0.3.)

The lamp has no direction indicator, and R6 is superseded by R148. (Device approval. Scope: This Regulation applies to direction indicators for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O, and T. Consolidated into UN R148. Spec terms 0.4, obligation base 0.0.)
